I've now viewed all 8 reference images across 8 different classes. Let me synthesize my analysis.

**Test image observations:**
- Green soybean pods on green stems
- Pods appear relatively normal, hairy, and green
- Background shows dried/brown plant material suggesting surrounding plants are more mature
- The plant itself remains fully green (both stems and pods)
- No lesions, spots, mold, or discoloration visible

**Analysis:**
The key diagnostic feature is that this plant remains entirely green (stems and pods) while the surrounding field appears to be maturing/senescing. This matches Green_stem_disorder, which is described as: "All or part of the soybean plant remains green while the rest of the plant or neighboring plants mature and senesce... Stems stay moist and green while pods may mature normally; plants may also stay green."

The reference image for Green_stem_disorder showed the mature-pod-on-green-stem variant, but the description also covers plants that stay entirely green. No other candidate matches: no mold (White_Mold), no dark spots (TSV, Anthracnose), no purple discoloration (Purple_Seed_Stain), no wilting (Phytophthora), no moldy seeds (Phomopsis).
